exhibits.label: Table 11.1
exhibits.title: Closed-loop variances in the Rudebusch-Svensson model, relative to TR93
exhibits.note: Unconditional variances of inflation, the output gap and the change in the policy rate under each rule, divided by their values under TR93; Mean averages the three. inf: unstable closed loop; rho: spectral radius of the closed loop. With RS99's unit-root Phillips curve a rule whose long-run inflation response is below one is unstable. Counterpart of Hinterlang & Tänzer (2021, Table 7) for the one backward-looking model.

exhibits.label: Figure 11.1
exhibits.title: Stable rules in the Rudebusch-Svensson model
exhibits.note: 5 of 17 rules give a stable closed loop. Rules to the lower left of TR93 reduce both variances.

exhibits.label: Table 11.2
exhibits.title: Effective Taylor coefficients of every trained policy
exhibits.note: OLS of the clipped policy rate on a grid over the observation, in the level form of Hinterlang & Tänzer (2021, Table 4); x2 policies carry fitted lag coefficients and a policy that observes the previous rate is evaluated with it held at 4 percent. Grouped by the economy the policy was trained in.

exhibits.label: Figure 11.2
exhibits.title: Best policy of each algorithm and the reference rules in the SVAR economy
exhibits.note: Simulated from the first two estimation-window quarters under freshly drawn shocks; every policy faces the same shocks within an economy. Not a historical counterfactual: the Actual line shares only its first two quarters with the simulations. For each algorithm the policy with the lowest loss in this economy is shown.

exhibits.title: Loss decomposition of every policy in its economy
exhibits.note: Mean squared deviations over the simulated quarters; Loss weights them as the reward does. Penalty is the mean footnote-13 term, so Loss + Penalty is minus the mean reward.
